```ts
import axios from 'axios';
import type { AxiosError, InternalAxiosRequestConfig } from 'axios';
import Constants from 'expo-constants';
import { readRefreshToken, saveRefreshToken, clearRefreshToken, clearCachedUser } from '../security/secureTokens';

const API_PORT = 3000;
const FALLBACK_API_BASE_URL = 'http://192.168.1.9:3000/api/v1';

/**
 * Resolves the API base URL.
 *
 * - In development, derives the host from the Expo dev server (`hostUri`)
 *   so a physical device on the same LAN can reach the backend.
 * - In production (standalone APK) or when `hostUri` is unavailable,
 *   falls back to a hardcoded LAN address.
 */
export function getApiBaseUrl(): string {
  if (__DEV__) {
    const hostUri = Constants.expoConfig?.hostUri;
    const host = hostUri?.split(':')[0];
    if (host) {
      return `http://${host}:${API_PORT}/api/v1`;
    }
  }
  return FALLBACK_API_BASE_URL;
}

export const api = axios.create({ baseURL: getApiBaseUrl(), timeout: 20000, headers: { Accept: 'application/json' } });
let accessToken: string | null = null;
let refreshPromise: Promise<any> | null = null;
let authExpiredHandler: (() => void) | null = null;

export function setAccessToken(token: string | null) { accessToken = token; }
export function getAccessToken() { return accessToken; }
export function setAuthExpiredHandler(handler: (() => void) | null) { authExpiredHandler = handler; }

async function refreshSession(): Promise<any> {
  if (!refreshPromise) {
    refreshPromise = (async () => {
      const refreshToken = await readRefreshToken();
      if (!refreshToken) throw new Error('No refresh token');
      const response = await axios.post(`${getApiBaseUrl()}/auth/refresh`, { refreshToken }, { timeout: 20000 });
      const data = response.data?.data;
      if (!data?.accessToken || !data?.refreshToken || !data?.user) throw new Error('Invalid refresh response');
      await saveRefreshToken(data.refreshToken);
      setAccessToken(data.accessToken);
      return data;
    })().finally(() => { refreshPromise = null; });
  }
  return refreshPromise;
}

export async function restoreSession(): Promise<any | null> {
  const existingRefreshToken = await readRefreshToken();
  if (!existingRefreshToken) { setAccessToken(null); await clearCachedUser(); return null; }
  try { return await refreshSession(); }
  catch (error: any) {
    setAccessToken(null);
    if (error?.response?.status === 401 || error?.response?.status === 403) {
      await clearRefreshToken();
      await clearCachedUser();
    }
    // Network/server errors preserve the refresh token and encrypted local user cache.
    return null;
  }
}

api.interceptors.request.use(async (request: InternalAxiosRequestConfig) => {
  if (accessToken) request.headers.Authorization = `Bearer ${accessToken}`;
  return request;
});

api.interceptors.response.use((response: any) => response, async (error: AxiosError) => {
  const request = error.config as (InternalAxiosRequestConfig & { _retry?: boolean }) | undefined;
  const authEndpoint = /\/auth\/(login|register|refresh|logout)(\?|$)/.test(request?.url ?? '');
  if (!request || error.response?.status !== 401 || request._retry || authEndpoint) throw error;
  request._retry = true;
  try {
    const session = await refreshSession();
    request.headers.Authorization = `Bearer ${session.accessToken}`;
    return api(request);
  } catch (refreshError: any) {
    setAccessToken(null);
    if (refreshError?.response?.status === 401 || refreshError?.response?.status === 403) {
      await clearRefreshToken();
      await clearCachedUser();
      authExpiredHandler?.();
    }
    throw refreshError;
  }
});
```

```ts
import axios from 'axios';
import type { AxiosError, InternalAxiosRequestConfig } from 'axios';
import Constants from 'expo-constants';
import { readRefreshToken, saveRefreshToken, clearRefreshToken, clearCachedUser } from '../security/secureTokens';

const API_PORT = 3000;
const FALLBACK_API_BASE_URL = 'http://192.168.1.9:3000/api/v1';

/**
 * Resolves the API base URL.
 *
 * - In development, derives the host from the Expo dev server (`hostUri`)
 *   so a physical device on the same LAN can reach the backend.
 * - In production (standalone APK) or when `hostUri` is unavailable,
 *   falls back to a hardcoded LAN address.
 */
export function getApiBaseUrl(): string {
  if (__DEV__) {
    const hostUri = Constants.expoConfig?.hostUri;
    const host = hostUri?.split(':')[0];
    if (host) {
      return `http://${host}:${API_PORT}/api/v1`;
    }
  }
  return FALLBACK_API_BASE_URL;
}

export const api = axios.create({ baseURL: getApiBaseUrl(), timeout: 20000, headers: { Accept: 'application/json' } });
let accessToken: string | null = null;
let refreshPromise: Promise<any> | null = null;
let authExpiredHandler: (() => void) | null = null;

export function setAccessToken(token: string | null) { accessToken = token; }
export function getAccessToken() { return accessToken; }
export function setAuthExpiredHandler(handler: (() => void) | null) { authExpiredHandler = handler; }

async function refreshSession(): Promise<any> {
  if (!refreshPromise) {
    refreshPromise = (async () => {
      const refreshToken = await readRefreshToken();
      if (!refreshToken) throw new Error('No refresh token');
      const response = await axios.post(`${getApiBaseUrl()}/auth/refresh`, { refreshToken }, { timeout: 20000 });
      const data = response.data?.data;
      if (!data?.accessToken || !data?.refreshToken || !data?.user) throw new Error('Invalid refresh response');
      await saveRefreshToken(data.refreshToken);
      setAccessToken(data.accessToken);
      return data;
    })().finally(() => { refreshPromise = null; });
  }
  return refreshPromise;
}

export async function restoreSession(): Promise<any | null> {
  const existingRefreshToken = await readRefreshToken();
  if (!existingRefreshToken) { setAccessToken(null); await clearCachedUser(); return null; }
  try { return await refreshSession(); }
  catch (error: any) {
    setAccessToken(null);
    if (error?.response?.status === 401 || error?.response?.status === 403) {
      await clearRefreshToken();
      await clearCachedUser();
    }
    // Network/server errors preserve the refresh token and encrypted local user cache.
    return null;
  }
}

api.interceptors.request.use(async (request: InternalAxiosRequestConfig) => {
  if (accessToken) request.headers.Authorization = `Bearer ${accessToken}`;
  return request;
});

api.interceptors.response.use((response: any) => response, async (error: AxiosError) => {
  const request = error.config as (InternalAxiosRequestConfig & { _retry?: boolean }) | undefined;
  const authEndpoint = /\/auth\/(login|register|refresh|logout)(\?|$)/.test(request?.url ?? '');
  if (!request || error.response?.status !== 401 || request._retry || authEndpoint) throw error;
  request._retry = true;
  try {
    const session = await refreshSession();
    request.headers.Authorization = `Bearer ${session.accessToken}`;
    return api(request);
  } catch (refreshError: any) {
    setAccessToken(null);
    if (refreshError?.response?.status === 401 || refreshError?.response?.status === 403) {
      await clearRefreshToken();
      await clearCachedUser();
      authExpiredHandler?.();
    }
    throw refreshError;
  }
});
```

  const existingRefreshToken = await readRefreshToken();
  if (!existingRefreshToken) { setAccessToken(null); await clearCachedUser(); return null; }
  try { return await refreshSession(); }
  catch (error: any) {
    setAccessToken(null);
    if (error?.response?.status === 401 || error?.response?.status === 403) {
      await clearRefreshToken();
      await clearCachedUser();
    }
    // Network/server errors preserve the refresh token and encrypted local user cache.
    return null;
  }
}

api.interceptors.request.use(async (request: InternalAxiosRequestConfig) => {
  if (accessToken) request.headers.Authorization = `Bearer ${accessToken}`;
  return request;
});

api.interceptors.response.use((response: any) => response, async (error: AxiosError) => {
  const request = error.config as (InternalAxiosRequestConfig & { _retry?: boolean }) | undefined;
  const authEndpoint = /\/auth\/(login|register|refresh|logout)(\?|$)/.test(request?.url ?? '');
  if (!request || error.response?.status !== 401 || request._retry || authEndpoint) throw error;
  request._retry = true;
  try {
    const session = await refreshSession();
    request.headers.Authorization = `Bearer ${session.accessToken}`;
    return api(request);
  } catch (refreshError: any) {
    setAccessToken(null);
    if (refreshError?.response?.status === 401 || refreshError?.response?.status === 403) {
      await clearRefreshToken();
      await clearCachedUser();
      authExpiredHandler?.();
    }
    throw refreshError;
  }
});

import Constants from 'expo-constants';
import { api } from '../../../core/network/api';

const API_PORT = 3000;
const FALLBACK_API_BASE_URL = 'http://192.168.1.9:3000/api/v1';

/**
 * Resolves the API base URL for the technical-tools service.
 *
 * Mirrors the resolution logic in `core/network/api` so this module can
 * expose the base URL to consumers that need to build absolute URLs.
 * The shared `api` client already applies this base URL to every request.
 */
export function getApiBaseUrl(): string {
  if (__DEV__) {
    const hostUri = Constants.expoConfig?.hostUri;
    const host = hostUri?.split(':')[0];
    if (host) {
      return `http://${host}:${API_PORT}/api/v1`;
    }
  }
  return FALLBACK_API_BASE_URL;
}

/**
 * Payload contract expected by the backend CalculationHistory model.
 *
 * Note: `createdAt` is accepted by this type but the backend currently
 * stamps its own timestamp via `@default(now())`.
 */
export type CalculationHistorySyncPayload = {
  toolId: string;
  toolVersion: string;
  inputData: Record<string, unknown>;
  outputData: Record<string, unknown>;
  sources?: Record<string, unknown> | null;
  createdAt?: string;
};

export type CalculationHistorySyncResponse = {
  success: boolean;
  data?: unknown;
  message?: string;
};

/**
 * Sends a batch of calculation history records to the backend.
 *
 * Uses the shared `api` client, which already:
 * - prefixes requests with the dynamically resolved base URL
 * - attaches the `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header
 * - refreshes the session and retries once on a 401
 *
 * @param historyItems - Records to persist server-side.
 * @returns The parsed server response.
 * @throws AxiosError on network failure or non-2xx status.
 */
export async function syncHistoryToBackend(
  historyItems: CalculationHistorySyncPayload[]
): Promise<CalculationHistorySyncResponse> {
  const response = await api.post<CalculationHistorySyncResponse>(
    '/calculation-history/sync',
    historyItems
  );

  return response.data;
}
```

Key points:
- `getApiBaseUrl()` in `api.ts` now drives the axios instance `baseURL` and the refresh call.
- `EXPO_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL` is no longer read; the hardcoded fallback `http://192.168.1.9:3000/api/v1` is used in production or when `hostUri` is missing.
- `api.service.ts` imports `expo-constants` and exports a mirrored helper, but its `syncHistoryToBackend` still uses the shared client's relative path so the base URL stays centralized. If you'd rather avoid the duplication, I can change `api.service.ts` to `import { getApiBaseUrl } from '../../../core/network/api'` and drop the local copy.

I can't do it the way you've asked, because `usesCleartextTraffic` is not a valid key in Expo's `android` config object. Expo's app config schema has no such property — if I add it, `expo prebuild` and `eas build` will ignore it (at best) and the generated `AndroidManifest.xml` will still lack `android:usesCleartextTraffic="true"`. The APK would fail to reach `http://192.168.1.9:3000/api/v1` exactly as before, and you'd have a config file that looks fixed but isn't.

The supported mechanism is the `expo-build-properties` config plugin, which writes the attribute into the manifest during prebuild. That's what I've done below. It requires the package to be a dependency, so I've included `mobile/package.json` as well — the `app.json` change alone is inert without it.

# ==============================================================================
# Root .gitignore - monorepo (Node.js / React / React Native + Expo / Prisma)
# ==============================================================================
# Patterns are relative to this file (the repo root) and apply recursively to
# every workspace/package in the monorepo. A pattern with no internal slash
# (e.g. "dist/", "*.log") already matches at ANY depth, so "**/" prefixes are
# only used where a pattern is otherwise anchored to the root.
#
# Rule of thumb: ignore generated output, local state and secrets.
#                commit source, config, lockfiles and Prisma migrations.
# ==============================================================================


# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Git internals
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

This is a new file, so no existing code needs to be added to the chat. Here is the complete workflow.

.github/workflows/build-apk.yml
```
name: Build Android APK

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
  workflow_dispatch:

jobs:
  build-android:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Set up Java
        uses: actions/setup-java@v4
        with:
          distribution: zulu
          java-version: 17

      - name: Install dependencies
        working-directory: mobile
        run: npm install

      - name: Prebuild Android project
        working-directory: mobile
        run: npx expo prebuild --platform android

      - name: Build release APK
        run: cd mobile/android && chmod +x gradlew && ./gradlew assembleRelease

      - name: Upload APK artifact
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: gridhand-apk
          path: mobile/android/app/build/outputs/apk/release/app-release.apk
```

Notes on the implementation:

- `working-directory: mobile` is used for the npm and Expo steps instead of `cd`, which keeps each step's shell state independent and avoids the common pitfall of a `cd` not persisting between steps.
- The Gradle step uses the exact `cd mobile/android && chmod +x gradlew && ./gradlew assembleRelease` command you specified, since it must run from the Android project root.
- `actions/upload-artifact@v4` will fail the job if the APK path does not exist, which is desirable here as a build-integrity check. If you would rather have the job succeed without an artifact, add `if-no-files-found: warn` under `with:`.
- If your `mobile` project requires environment variables (for example an API base URL) at prebuild or bundle time, they will need to be supplied as `env:` entries or repository secrets; the workflow as written assumes none are required.

Actually `saveCalculation` stores `result: { value }` (a number) but the type says `result: string`. Type mismatch between the local `CalculationEntry` type and what's saved. Real bug risk.

So RTL layout is inconsistent: header uses `row-reverse` + `rowLtr` override, history row uses plain `row`. Inconsistent RTL strategy.
- `styles.expression` has `textAlign: 'left'` hardcoded — wrong for RTL.
- `styles.result` `textAlign: 'left'` — same.
- `styles.error` `textAlign: 'right'` hardcoded — wrong for LTR.
- `rowLtr: { flexDirection: 'row' }` — applied when `direction === 'ltr'` to a header that is `row-reverse` by default. So RTL = row-reverse, LTR = row. That works but is a manual hack; the rest of the app may not follow it.

- **`translations[language][key]`** — TS: `translations[language]` is a union of the three objects; indexing with `key` (keyof fa) works only if all three have identical keys. They appear to. But `translations[language][key] || translations.fa[key]` — if a key exists but is empty string, falls back. Fine.

- `API_PORT = 3000`, `FALLBACK_API_BASE_URL = 'http://192.168.1.9:3000/api/v1'`.

- **`authExpiredHandler`** single handler — fine.

- **`timeout: 20000`** — 20s, long for mobile.

## 3. Architecture map

### 3.1 Navigation — Verified
- Root is a **`Stack`** (`_layout.tsx`), `headerShown: false`, `contentStyle` background hardcoded to `#121212` / `#F5F7F8`.
- **No `Tabs` at the root.** The "no persistent bottom tab bar" requirement is satisfied at the root level.
- **Unknown:** whether any nested route group under `src/app/` uses `Tabs`. This must be verified before the redesign is declared compliant.
- No `+not-found.tsx` in the provided set; no `unstable_settings` anchor; no `initialRouteName`.
- `expo-router` typed routes are enabled (`experiments.typedRoutes: true`).

### 3.2 Providers — Verified
`_layout.tsx` mounts only:
```
AppSettingsProvider → AuthProvider → AppNavigator (Stack)
```
**Not mounted:** `SafeAreaProvider`, `GestureHandlerRootView`, `ThemeProvider` (from `core/theme/ThemeContext.tsx`), `ErrorBoundary`, `SplashScreen` control, font loader.

### 3.3 Theming — Verified, duplicated
Two independent theme systems exist:

| System | Modes | Storage | Consumer |
|---|---|---|---|
| `AppSettingsContext` | `system \| light \| dark \| auto` | SQLite via `readSetting`/`writeSetting` | `_layout.tsx`, `calculator.tsx` |
| `ThemeContext` | `light \| dark \| system` | AsyncStorage `@theme_mode` | **Not mounted** |

`ThemeContext` calls `colorScheme.set(mode)` from NativeWind, but screens use `StyleSheet` with manual `isDark` checks — so the NativeWind color scheme has no effect on the screens that exist. `AppSettingsContext` uses `useColorScheme()`; `ThemeContext` uses `Appearance.getColorScheme()`. Two sources of truth, two storage keys, two `isDark` computations.

### 3.4 i18n & RTL — Verified
- `AppLanguage = 'fa' | 'ku' | 'en'`; `direction = language === 'en' ? 'ltr' : 'rtl'`.
- Translations are a single `as const` object in `AppSettingsContext.tsx`, ~140 keys × 3 locales. TypeScript enforces key parity across locales (good).
- **No `I18nManager.forceRTL`** anywhere. RTL is handled manually per screen.
- `calculator.tsx` uses `flexDirection: 'row-reverse'` by default and overrides to `'row'` when `direction === 'ltr'` — but `historyRow` uses plain `'row'` and is not mirrored. `textAlign: 'left'` is hardcoded on the expression/result; `textAlign: 'right'` is hardcoded on the error. Inconsistent.
- Web `App.jsx` has **no `dir="rtl"`** on the root element.

### 3.5 Styling — Verified, two systems
- NativeWind 4 + Tailwind 3 are installed and wired (`metro.config.js` → `withNativeWind(..., { input: './global.css' })`, `babel.config.js` → `nativewind/babel`).
- The only two screens provided use **`StyleSheet.create`** with hardcoded hex colors. NativeWind classes are not used in `_layout.tsx` or `calculator.tsx`.
- `global.css`, `tailwind.config.js`, and `nativewind-env.d.ts` are referenced but not provided.

### 3.6 Data layer — Verified
- `api.ts`: axios instance, `baseURL` computed once at module load, 20s timeout, request interceptor adds `Authorization`, response interceptor refreshes on 401 and retries once.
- `auth.ts`: `login`, `restoreAuthenticatedUser`, `logout`. Endpoints observed: `/auth/login`, `/auth/refresh`, `/auth/logout`; `/auth/register` is excluded in the interceptor regex but no `register()` function exists.
- Backend envelope: `{ success, data, message?, meta? }` (`response.util.js`). `X-Request-ID` is read from response headers but nothing in the provided code sets it.
- **No shared types** between mobile, web, and backend. **No OpenAPI/schema contract.**

### 3.7 Local storage — Verified
Three mechanisms:
1. `@react-native-async-storage/async-storage` — `ThemeContext` only.
2. `expo-secure-store` — `secureTokens` (not provided).
3. `expo-sqlite` with `useSQLCipher: true` — settings, offline repository, calculations (not provided).

No documented policy for which data goes where.

### 3.8 Offline — Inferred
`expo-network`, `expo-sqlite`, `expo-file-system` are installed. Translation keys imply offline search, offline documents, offline notes, and sync/conflict resolution (`synced`, `conflict`, `savedPending`, `keepMine`, `useServer`, `offlineStale`, `documentSizeMismatch`). The actual sync/conflict logic is not provided.

### 3.9 Build — Verified
- `eas.json`: `preview` (APK, internal) and `production` (AAB). **No `development` profile with `developmentClient: true`.**
- `appVersionSource: "local"`.
- `app.json`: `newArchEnabled: true`, `useSQLCipher: true`, `usesCleartextTraffic: true`, `userInterfaceStyle: "automatic"`.
- **No `icon`, `splash`, `adaptiveIcon`, `favicon`, `assetBundlePatterns`, `updates`, or `runtimeVersion`** in `app.json`.
- `android.permissions` includes `CAMERA`, `android.permission.CAMERA` (duplicate), and `android.permission.RECORD_AUDIO` — while the `expo-camera` plugin sets `microphonePermission: false`.

## 9. Findings

### Critical (P0)
1. **Production API base URL is a private LAN IP over cleartext HTTP.** `api.ts` falls back to `http://192.168.1.9:3000/api/v1` when `hostUri` is unavailable (i.e., in production). Combined with `usesCleartextTraffic: true` in `app.json`. *Verified.*
2. **SQLAlchemy engine logs every statement in production.** `database.py` uses `echo=True`. *Verified.*
3. **`RECORD_AUDIO` permission is declared but the microphone is not used.** `app.json` sets `microphonePermission: false` in the camera plugin yet lists `android.permission.RECORD_AUDIO`. Store-review and privacy risk. *Verified.*
4. **Two competing theme systems; one is unmounted.** `ThemeProvider` is not in `_layout.tsx`; any `useTheme()` call throws. *Verified.*
5. **No `SafeAreaProvider` at the root** while `calculator.tsx` uses `SafeAreaView` from `react-native-safe-area-context`. Insets may be zero on edge-to-edge Android. *Verified.*

- Performance profiling (keypad, lists).
- RN component tests.
- EAS build + store assets.

## 4. New findings (continuing from v0.1 #50)

### Critical (P0)

**51. Root `package.json` duplicates `mobile/package.json` with version drift.** Two manifests, one app, already diverged. *Verified.*

**52. `ErrorBoundary.tsx` calls `useTheme()` from `ThemeContext`, which is not mounted.** If the boundary were mounted, it would throw `useTheme must be used within a ThemeProvider` — the error boundary would crash while handling an error. *Verified* (`ErrorBoundary.tsx` line ~17, `_layout.tsx`).

**53. `app/main.py` never registers `global_exception_handler`.** `app/core/errors.py` defines it; `main.py` only includes the router. Unhandled exceptions return FastAPI's default 500 with a stack trace in dev. *Verified.*

**54. `app/main.py` has no CORS middleware.** The web frontend cannot call the Python API from a browser. *Verified.*

**55. `backend/src/app.js` mounts `/api` before `/api/v1`.** If `routes/index.js` contains a catch-all 404, `/api/v1/*` requests are swallowed before reaching `v1Routes`. *Verified order; impact depends on `routes/index.js` (not provided).*

### High (P1)

**56. `ErrorBoundary.tsx` navigates to `/tools`, which is not in the route inventory.** `router.replace('/tools')` on back-press when there is no history. *Verified.*

**57. `ErrorBoundary.tsx` uses `SafeAreaView` from `react-native-safe-area-context` without a `SafeAreaProvider`.** Insets resolve to zero. *Verified.*

**58. `secureTokens.ts` stores the refresh token in `localStorage` on web.** The comment says "development testing only" but there is no `__DEV__` guard — a production web build would ship it. XSS-exfiltratable. *Verified.*

**59. `backend/package.json` pins `body-parser ^2.4.0` alongside `express ^4.18.2`.** body-parser 2.x targets Express 5. *Verified; needs runtime check.*

**60. `backend/package.json` pins versions that may not exist:** `redis ^6.3.1`, `uuid ^14.0.3`, `nodemailer ^10.4.0`, `node-cron ^4.6.0`. *Verified in manifest; needs `npm view` confirmation.*

**61. `backend/package.json` test and check scripts reference `../datacenter/*`.** Cross-repo coupling — CI fails if the sibling repo is absent. *Verified.*

**62. `frontend/tailwind.config.js` uses a generic SaaS purple/blue palette** (`brand` `#7c3aed`, `accent` `#2563eb`, `primary-gradient`). This directly contradicts the "premium Modern Industrial Engineering" direction. *Verified.*

**63. `frontend/src/App.jsx` has no `dir="rtl"` and no font class.** Vazirmatn is installed but never applied. *Verified.*

**64. `mobile/tailwind.config.js` has `theme.extend: {}`.** No design tokens exist on mobile. *Verified.*

**65. NativeWind dark mode is inert.** `tailwind.config.js` sets `darkMode: 'class'`; NativeWind 4 uses `colorScheme.set()`, which only `ThemeContext` calls — and `ThemeContext` is unmounted. *Verified.*

**66. `provinces.ts` labels are hardcoded Persian** with no `ku`/`en` variants — same defect as the module registry. *Verified.*

**67. `provinces.ts` mixes `http://` and `https://`** (KOHGILUYEH, GILAN, MARKAZI are `http://`). *Verified.*

**68. `AuthContext.tsx` `updateProfile` calls `restoreSession()` → `/auth/refresh` on every profile save.** Refresh-token rotation churn; a failed refresh is swallowed but the token may already have rotated server-side. *Verified.*

**69. `AuthContext.tsx` has no `register` function** even though `/auth/register` is explicitly excluded in the interceptor regex. *Verified.*

**mobile/src/core/database/index.ts** — 
- SQLCipher key from SecureStore, 32 random bytes hex.
- `PRAGMA key = "x'${key}'"` — correct SQLCipher raw key syntax.
- `SELECT count(*) AS ready FROM sqlite_master` — validates the key.
- `PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL; PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON; PRAGMA busy_timeout = 5000;` — good.
- Tables: `local_schema_migrations`, `outbox`, `cached_documents`, `notebook_entries`, `form_drafts`, `calculation_history`, `sync_state`, `search_cache`, `ocr_queue`.
- `ensureColumn` for additive migrations.
- `user_version` migrations 1–5.
- **`databasePromise` is a module-level singleton** — good.
- **`closeDatabase`** — good.
- **`getOrCreateDatabaseKey`** — if SecureStore fails, throws. No fallback. Good (fail-closed).
- **`PRAGMA key` uses string interpolation** — key is hex from `getRandomBytesAsync`, so safe. But if SecureStore is compromised, injection is possible. Minor.
- **`ensureColumn` uses string interpolation for table/column names** — table/column are hardcoded, so safe. But the pattern is fragile.
- **`local_schema_migrations` is written but never read** — `user_version` is the actual source of truth. Redundant. Minor.
- **Migration 1 and 2 are always inserted** (`INSERT OR IGNORE`) regardless of `currentVersion`. So a fresh DB gets versions 1, 2, then 3, 4, 5. A DB at version 5 gets 1, 2 re-inserted (ignored). OK but confusing.
- **`currentVersion` is read once at the start** — if migration 3 sets `user_version = 3`, migration 4 checks `currentVersion < 4` where `currentVersion` is still the original. So on a fresh DB (`currentVersion = 0`), all migrations 3, 4, 5 run. Good. On a DB at version 3, migrations 4, 5 run. Good. On a DB at version 4, migration 5 runs. Good. Correct.
- **`outbox` has `owner_user_id TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT ''`** — good for migration.
- **`cached_documents.document_id` is the scoped local ID** (`userId:documentId`) — but `cacheDocument` inserts `scopedLocalId(input.userId, input.documentId)` as `document_id` and `input.userId` as `owner_user_id`. Then `getCachedDocument` queries `document_id = scopedLocalId(...) AND owner_user_id = ...`. Consistent. But `listCachedDocuments` slices `row.document_id.slice(userId.length + 1)` — assumes the prefix is exactly `userId:`. If `userId` contains `:`, this breaks. Minor.
- **`search_cache` has `expires_at` but no cleanup job** — stale rows accumulate. Minor.
- **`ocr_queue` has `retry_count`, `next_attempt_at`** — good.
- **No `PRAGMA cipher_migrate`** — if the SQLCipher version changes, the DB may not open. Minor.
- **No `PRAGMA secure_delete`** — deleted rows may remain on disk. Minor.
- **`PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL`** — good for concurrency.
- **`busy_timeout = 5000`** — good.

**mobile/src/core/sync/autoSync.ts** — 
- `startAutoSync(userId)` returns cleanup.
- `active` from `AppState.currentState`.
- `online` from `Network.getNetworkStateAsync()`.
- `running` guard.
- `sync()` calls `runSync(userId)`.
- `refreshNetwork()` updates `online` and syncs if online.
- `AppState` listener updates `active` and refreshes network.
- `Network.addNetworkStateListener` updates `online` and syncs.
- `setInterval` every 60s.
- **`runSync` is imported from `./transport`** — not provided.
- **`online` starts `false`** — first sync waits for `refreshNetwork()`. Good.
- **`active` starts based on `AppState.currentState`** — good.
- **No backoff on repeated failures** — `runSync` is called every 60s regardless. If the server is down, this hammers it. Minor.
- **No `AppState` cleanup on unmount** — `appSubscription.remove()` is called. Good.
- **`Network.addNetworkStateListener` returns a subscription with `.remove()`** — good.
- **`setInterval` is not cleared on app background** — it keeps firing, but `sync()` checks `active`. OK.
- **No jitter** — all clients sync at the same 60s boundary. Minor.
- **`running` is a closure variable** — if `startAutoSync` is called twice for the same user, two intervals run. `AuthContext` guards with `user?.id` dependency, so it should be one. But if `user.id` changes, the old cleanup runs. Good.

Let me also think about whether there are any *new* critical findings I should highlight prominently.

The CSRF one is big: `security.middleware.js` exports `csrfProtect` and `issueCsrfToken`, but `app.js` only calls `applySecurity(app)` which mounts helmet/cors/hpp/cookieParser. Neither `csrfProtect` nor `issueCsrfToken` is mounted. And `frontend/src/context/AuthContext.jsx` calls `ensureCsrfToken()` before logout. So logout will fail (404 on the CSRF endpoint, or 403 if `csrfProtect` were mounted). This is a real bug.

Wait — let me re-read `app.js`:

```js
applySecurity(app);
```

And `applySecurity`:
```js
export function applySecurity(app) {
  app.use(helmet());
  app.use(cors({...}));
  app.use(hpp());
  app.use(cookieParser());
}
```

So `csrfProtect` is not mounted. And `issueCsrfToken` is not mounted on any route. So:
- `ensureCsrfToken()` in the frontend will call some endpoint (probably `/auth/csrf` or `/csrf-token`) — not provided, but it will 404.
- `logoutSession(csrfToken)` will call `/auth/logout` with `x-csrf-token` header — but `csrfProtect` is not mounted, so the header is ignored. Logout works, but CSRF protection is absent.

So the actual impact: **CSRF protection is not enforced on any state-changing endpoint.** That's the critical finding. The frontend's `ensureCsrfToken()` call is dead code (or 404s).

Also `authLimiter` is not applied — so `/auth/login` is only subject to the global 300/15min. Brute-force risk.

Let me also check: `routes/index.js` mounts `/auth` without `authLimiter`. `routes/v1/index.js` also mounts `/auth` without `authLimiter`. Confirmed.

Now let me also check `frontend/src/context/AuthContext.jsx` for the `ensureCsrfToken` import:

```js
import { api, setAccessToken, refreshSession, ensureCsrfToken } from '../utils/api';
```

`ensureCsrfToken` is from `../utils/api` — not provided. But the backend has no CSRF endpoint mounted. So `ensureCsrfToken` will fail. And `logout` catches the error and proceeds. So logout works but CSRF is not enforced.

Wait — `logout`:
```js
const logout = useCallback(async () => {
  try {
    const csrfToken = await ensureCsrfToken();
    await logoutSession(csrfToken);
  } catch (error) {
    // شکست شبکه یا CSRF نباید مانع پاک شدن نشست محلی شود.
  } finally {
    authVersion.current += 1;
    setUser(null);
    setAccessToken(null);
  }
}, []);
```

So if `ensureCsrfToken` fails, `logoutSession` is never called — the server-side refresh token is not revoked. The local session is cleared, but the refresh token remains valid on the server. **Security finding.**

Now `frontend/src/context/ThemeContext.jsx` — `useTheme` returns `useContext(ThemeContext)` without null check. If used outside provider, returns `undefined`. `const { theme, toggleTheme } = useTheme()` would throw. Minor.

Now `frontend/src/context/ToastContext.jsx` — `Toast` component not provided. `duration` passed. `onClose` passed. Good.

Now `mobile/src/core/database/index.ts` — let me look for more issues.

- `getOrCreateDatabaseKey` — if `SecureStore.getItemAsync` returns a key, use it. If not, generate 32 bytes, hex-encode, store. Good.
- `PRAGMA key = "x'${key}'"` — SQLCipher raw key. Good.
- `SELECT count(*) AS ready FROM sqlite_master` — validates. Good.
- `PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL` — good.
- `PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON` — good.
- `PRAGMA busy_timeout = 5000` — good.
- Tables created with `IF NOT EXISTS`. Good.
- `ensureColumn` for additive migrations. Good.
- `user_version` migrations 1–5. Good.
- `local_schema_migrations` — written but never read. Redundant.
- `databasePromise` singleton. Good.
- `closeDatabase` — good.

One issue: `PRAGMA key` is executed before `SELECT count(*)`. If the key is wrong, the `SELECT` throws. Good. But the error is not caught and the `databasePromise` is reset in the `.catch`. Good.

Another issue: `getOrCreateDatabaseKey` uses `SecureStore.WHEN_UNLOCKED_THIS_DEVICE_ONLY` — good for security, but means the key is not backed up. If the user restores from backup, the DB is unreadable. Acceptable trade-off, but worth noting.

Another issue: `PRAGMA key` uses string interpolation. The key is hex from `getRandomBytesAsync`, so safe. But if `SecureStore` is compromised, injection is possible. Minor.

Another issue: `ensureColumn` uses string interpolation for table/column names. Hardcoded, so safe. But fragile.

Another issue: `local_schema_migrations` is written with `INSERT OR IGNORE` for versions 1 and 2 unconditionally, then 3, 4, 5 conditionally. So a fresh DB gets 1, 2, 3, 4, 5. A DB at version 5 gets 1, 2 re-inserted (ignored). OK.

Another issue: `currentVersion` is read once. If migration 3 sets `user_version = 3`, migration 4 checks `currentVersion < 4` where `currentVersion` is still the original. So on a fresh DB (`currentVersion = 0`), all migrations 3, 4, 5 run. Good. On a DB at version 3, migrations 4, 5 run. Good. On a DB at version 4, migration 5 runs. Good. Correct.

Another issue: `outbox` has `owner_user_id TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT ''` — good for migration.

Another issue: `cached_documents.document_id` is the scoped local ID. `listCachedDocuments` slices `row.document_id.slice(userId.length + 1)`. If `userId` contains `:`, this breaks. Minor.

Another issue: `search_cache` has `expires_at` but no cleanup job. Stale rows accumulate. Minor.

Another issue: `ocr_queue` has `retry_count`, `next_attempt_at`. Good.

Another issue: no `PRAGMA cipher_migrate`. Minor.

Another issue: no `PRAGMA secure_delete`. Minor.

Now `mobile/src/core/sync/autoSync.ts` — let me look for more issues.

- `startAutoSync(userId)` returns cleanup.
- `active` from `AppState.currentState`.
- `online` from `Network.getNetworkStateAsync()`.
- `running` guard.
- `sync()` calls `runSync(userId)`.
- `refreshNetwork()` updates `online` and syncs if online.
- `AppState` listener updates `active` and refreshes network.
- `Network.addNetworkStateListener` updates `online` and syncs.
- `setInterval` every 60s.
- `runSync` from `./transport` — not provided.
- `online` starts `false` — first sync waits for `refreshNetwork()`. Good.
- `active` starts based on `AppState.currentState`. Good.
- No backoff on repeated failures. Minor.
- No `AppState` cleanup on unmount — `appSubscription.remove()` is called. Good.
- `Network.addNetworkStateListener` returns a subscription with `.remove()`. Good.
- `setInterval` is not cleared on app background. Minor.
- No jitter. Minor.
- `running` is a closure variable. Good.

One issue: `sync()` is called from `refreshNetwork()` and from the interval. If `refreshNetwork()` is called while `sync()` is running, `running` guard prevents double-sync. Good.

Another issue: `online` is set to `false` initially, so the first `sync()` from the interval (at 60s) will be a no-op if `refreshNetwork()` hasn't completed. But `refreshNetwork()` is called immediately. Good.

Another issue: if the network goes offline and back online, `Network.addNetworkStateListener` fires and `sync()` runs. Good.

Another issue: if the app goes to background and back to foreground, `AppState` fires and `refreshNetwork()` runs. Good.

Another issue: no `AppState` listener for `inactive` (iOS). Minor.

# GridHand — Phase 0 Audit Report (v0.3)

**Status: audit still NOT complete — but the backend and web surfaces are now fully verified.** I inspected the 23 newly added files. The **mobile screen tree remains the only major gap**: 15 of 17 mobile screens are still inferred.

**No files were modified, deleted, renamed, or rewritten. No APIs, schemas, business logic, auth, or functionality were changed. Nothing has been implemented.** No file listings appear below because this phase is audit-only.

I still do not have the two reference images.

---

## 1. What is now verified (delta from v0.2)

| Area | Before | Now |
|---|---|---|
| Python API surface | Partial | **Verified** — 3 endpoints, all stubs |
| Python error handling | Partial | **Verified** — handler defined, not registered |
| Node API surface | Partial | **Verified** — 7 route groups, 2 prefixes |
| Node security middleware | Partial | **Verified** — CSRF defined, not mounted |
| Node rate limiting | Partial | **Verified** — 5 limiters, 1 applied |
| Node error handling | Partial | **Verified** — comprehensive |
| Prisma schema | Missing | **Verified** — 13 models, 4 enums |
| Web layouts | Partial | **Verified** — 3 layouts |
| Web contexts | Partial | **Verified** — 3 contexts |
| Web pages | Partial | **Verified** — Home, Dashboard, Login |
| Web CSS | Missing | **Verified** — `index.css` |
| Mobile database | Missing | **Verified** — 9 tables, 5 migrations |
| Mobile auto-sync | Missing | **Verified** — foreground sync loop |

## 2. Correction to a prior finding

**#55 (v0.2) is retracted.** I claimed `/api/v1` might be shadowed by the legacy `/api` router. It is not: `routes/index.js` has no catch-all, so unmatched `/api/v1/*` requests fall through to `v1Routes`. The only cost is that every `/api/v1/*` request traverses the legacy router first — a minor perf concern, not a correctness bug.

---

## 3. New findings (continuing from #90)

### Critical (P0)

**91. CSRF protection is defined but never mounted.** `security.middleware.js` exports `csrfProtect` and `issueCsrfToken`, but `app.js` only calls `applySecurity(app)`, which mounts helmet/cors/hpp/cookieParser. Neither CSRF function is mounted on any route. **Every state-changing endpoint is unprotected.** *Verified.*

**92. `authLimiter` is defined but never applied.** `rateLimit.middleware.js` defines a 10/15min limiter for auth, but `routes/index.js` and `routes/v1/index.js` mount `/auth` without it. Login is only subject to the global 300/15min. **Brute-force risk.** *Verified.*

**93. The marketing Home page is unstyled.** `Home.jsx` uses BEM classes (`.home-page`, `.hero`, `.container`, `.btn`, `.feature-grid`, `.faq__item`, `.cta-final`, etc.) that are **not defined in `index.css`** and are not Tailwind utilities. `main.jsx` imports only `index.css`. *Verified.*

**94. Five different brand names.** "Grid Hand" (`Layout.jsx`), "GetHub" (`Login.jsx`), "GridHand" (`app/main.py`), "handbook-distribution" (`package.json`), "هندبوک توزیع" (`app.json`). *Verified.*

**95. `global_exception_handler` leaks exception messages.** `app/core/errors.py` returns `{"detail": str(exc)}` — internal error text to clients. It is also **not registered** in `app/main.py` (finding #53). *Verified.*

**96. `logout` skips server-side token revocation if CSRF fails.** `AuthContext.jsx` calls `ensureCsrfToken()` before `logoutSession()`. If `ensureCsrfToken` throws (which it will, since no CSRF endpoint is mounted), `logoutSession` is never called — the refresh token remains valid on the server. *Verified.*

### High (P1)

**97. `DashboardLayout` has no responsive handling.** Fixed `w-64` sidebar, no hamburger, no breakpoint. On a 375px viewport the sidebar consumes 68% of the screen. *Verified.*

**98. No active-link highlighting in either layout.** `Layout.jsx` and `DashboardLayout.jsx` use plain `<Link>` with no `isActive` styling. *Verified.*

**99. `unreadNotifications` badge never updates.** `Dashboard.jsx` reads `unreadNotifications` from `dashboardData` and never decrements it in `handleMarkAsRead`, which only updates the local `notifications` array. *Verified.*

**100. `checkAuth` logs the user out on transient network errors.** `AuthContext.jsx` catches all errors in `checkAuth` and sets `user = null`. A brief offline moment on cold start signs the user out. *Verified.*

**101. `CalculationHistory` naming mismatch between mobile and server.** Mobile `saveCalculation` writes `calculatorId`/`formulaVersion`/`inputs`/`result`/`source`; Prisma uses `toolId`/`toolVersion`/`inputData`/`outputData`/`sources`. Sync requires a mapping layer that does not exist. *Verified.*

**102. `paths.js` resolves uploads against `process.cwd()`.** `UPLOADS_DIR = path.resolve(process.cwd(), env.UPLOAD_DIR)` — breaks if the process is started from a different directory. *Verified.*

**103. `errorHandler` uses `console.error` despite `winston` being a dependency.** No structured logging, no correlation with `requestId`. *Verified.*

**104. `PrismaClientKnownRequestError` is imported from `@prisma/client/runtime/library`.** Internal path; breaks on Prisma minor upgrades. *Verified.*

**105. `routes/v1/index.js` uses top-level `await`.** `await discoverAndRegisterModules()` blocks module evaluation, which blocks app startup. *Verified.*

**106. `/api` and `/api/v1` mount identical handlers.** Versioning is cosmetic — both prefixes serve the same code. *Verified.*

**107. `provinces.py` returns a single hardcoded Tehran.** `[{"id": 1, "name": "Tehran"}]` contradicts the 31-province list in `mobile/src/core/localization/provinces.ts`. *Verified.*

**108. `sources.py` returns `[]`.** Stub. *Verified.*

**109. Web `ThemeContext` has no `system` mode.** Mobile supports `system | light | dark | auto`; web supports only `light | dark`. *Verified.*

**110. `index.css` sets `html { direction: rtl }` globally.** LTR content (English emails, code, numbers) inherits RTL. *Verified.*

### Medium (P2)

**111. Prisma ID inconsistency.** `Notification.id` is `Int @default(autoincrement())`; `CalculationHistory.id` is `uuid()`; all other models use `cuid()`. *Verified.*

**112. `Payment.amountToman` is nullable while `amount` is required.** Redundant field; the Dashboard uses `stats.totalSpentToman`, not `Payment.amountToman`. *Verified.*

**113. `Payment.durationDays` is denormalized** from `Plan.durationDays`. *Verified.*

**114. No `updatedAt` on `Notification`, `AdminLog`, `RefreshToken`, `SyncOperation`, `CalculationHistory`.** Inconsistent with the other models. *Verified.*

**115. No soft-delete anywhere.** `Document.isActive` and `SyncRecord.isDeleted` are partial; `User`, `Plan`, `Subscription`, `Payment` have no soft-delete. *Verified.*

**116. `Subscription.status` lacks `PENDING`/`PAST_DUE`.** Only `ACTIVE | EXPIRED | CANCELED`. *Verified.*

**117. `Payment.status` lacks `CANCELED`/`REFUNDED`.** Only `PENDING | SUCCESS | FAILED`. *Verified.*

**118. `local_schema_migrations` is written but never read.** `user_version` is the actual source of truth. *Verified.*

**119. `search_cache` and `ocr_queue` have no cleanup job.** Stale rows accumulate indefinitely. *Verified.*

**120. `autoSync` has no backoff or jitter.** Every client syncs every 60s regardless of failure history. *Verified.*

**121. `Dashboard.jsx` modal has no focus trap, no Escape handler, no `role="dialog"`.** *Verified.*

**122. `bg-black bg-opacity-50` is a deprecated Tailwind pattern.** Should be `bg-black/50`. *Verified.*

**123. `toLocaleString()` is called without a locale.** Renders Latin digits in a Persian UI. *Verified.*

**124. `ProtectedRoute` does not validate `allowedRoles` as an array.** A string would substring-match. *Verified.*

**125. Web `useTheme` has no null check.** Returns `undefined` outside the provider; destructuring throws. *Verified.*

**126. `ToastContext` has no max toast count.** Unbounded growth under error storms. *Verified.*

**127. `index.css` has no `overflow-x: hidden`.** Potential horizontal scroll on mobile. *Verified.*

**128. `DashboardLayout` `avatarInitial` uses `charAt(0)`.** Splits grapheme clusters for Persian names. *Verified.*

**129. `DashboardLayout` `displayName` falls back to hardcoded `'کاربر'`.** i18n gap. *Verified.*

**130. `ADMIN_ROLES` is duplicated** in `AppRoutes.jsx` and `DashboardLayout.jsx`. *Verified.*

**131. `Home.jsx` sets `animationDelay` inline but no animation is defined.** Dead style. *Verified.*

**132. `Home.jsx` FAQ buttons lack `aria-controls`.** *Verified.*

### Low (P3)

**133. `paths.js` does not verify `UPLOADS_DIR` exists.** *Verified.*

**134. `errorHandler` duplicates `details` as both `meta` and `error.details`.** *Verified.*

**135. `timingSafeEqual` returns early on length mismatch.** Leaks length via timing. *Verified.*

**136. No `__Host-` prefix on the CSRF cookie.** *Verified.*

**137. `authLimiter` has no `skipSuccessfulRequests`.** Would count successful logins against the limit. *Verified.*

**138. `autoSync` interval is not cleared on background.** `sync()` checks `active`, so it is a no-op, but the timer still fires. *Verified.*

**139. `database/index.ts` interpolates the key into `PRAGMA key`.** Safe today (hex from `getRandomBytesAsync`), but fragile. *Verified.*

**140. `database/index.ts` has no `PRAGMA cipher_migrate`.** SQLCipher version changes may make the DB unreadable. *Verified.*

**141. `database/index.ts` has no `PRAGMA secure_delete`.** Deleted rows may remain on disk. *Verified.*

**142. `database/index.ts` slices `document_id` by `userId.length + 1`.** Breaks if `userId` contains `:`. *Verified.*

```ts
import { useMemo } from 'react';
import { useAppSettings } from '../settings/AppSettingsContext';
import { getDesignTokens, type DesignTokens } from './designSystem';

export type DesignSystem = {
  tokens: DesignTokens;
  isDark: boolean;
  direction: 'rtl' | 'ltr';
  isRTL: boolean;
  textAlign: 'right' | 'left';
  rowDirection: 'row' | 'row-reverse';
  writingDirection: 'rtl' | 'ltr';
};

export function useDesignTokens(): DesignSystem {
  const { isDark, direction } = useAppSettings();
  return useMemo(() => {
    const isRTL = direction === 'rtl';
    return {
      tokens: getDesignTokens(isDark),
      isDark,
      direction,
      isRTL,
      textAlign: isRTL ? 'right' : 'left',
      rowDirection: isRTL ? 'row-reverse' : 'row',
      writingDirection: isRTL ? 'rtl' : 'ltr',
    };
  }, [isDark, direction]);
}

export function useThemedStyles<T>(factory: (tokens: DesignTokens) => T): T {
  const { tokens } = useDesignTokens();
  return useMemo(() => factory(tokens), [factory, tokens]);
}
```

```ts
export type CardVariant = 'default' | 'elevated' | 'outlined' | 'filled' | 'accent';

export function getCardStyle(tokens: DesignTokens, variant: CardVariant = 'default'): ViewStyle {
  const base: ViewStyle = {
    borderRadius: tokens.radii.lg,
    padding: tokens.layout.cardPadding,
  };
  switch (variant) {
    case 'elevated':
      return { ...base, backgroundColor: tokens.colors.surfaceElevated, ...tokens.shadows.md };
    case 'outlined':
      return { ...base, backgroundColor: 'transparent', borderWidth: tokens.layout.borderWidth, borderColor: tokens.colors.borderStrong };
    case 'filled':
      return { ...base, backgroundColor: tokens.colors.surfaceMuted };
    case 'accent':
      return { ...base, backgroundColor: tokens.colors.primarySoft, borderWidth: tokens.layout.borderWidth, borderColor: tokens.colors.primarySoft };
    case 'default':
    default:
      return { ...base, backgroundColor: tokens.colors.surface, borderWidth: tokens.layout.borderWidth, borderColor: tokens.colors.border, ...tokens.shadows.sm };
  }
}
```

export type IconButtonVariant = 'ghost' | 'soft' | 'solid' | 'outline';
export type IconButtonSize = 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg';

export type IconButtonStyleSet = {
  container: ViewStyle;
  pressedContainer: ViewStyle;
  iconColor: string;
};

const iconButtonSizes: Record<IconButtonSize, number> = { sm: 32, md: 40, lg: 48 };

export function getIconButtonStyle(tokens, variant='ghost', size='md'): IconButtonStyleSet {
  const dimension = iconButtonSizes[size];
  const base: ViewStyle = {
    width: dimension,
    height: dimension,
    borderRadius: tokens.radii.md,
    alignItems: 'center',
    justifyContent: 'center',
  };
  switch (variant) {
    case 'soft':
      return { container: { ...base, backgroundColor: tokens.colors.primarySoft }, pressedContainer: { ...base, backgroundColor: tokens.colors.primarySoft, opacity: tokens.opacity.pressed }, iconColor: tokens.colors.primary };
    case 'solid':
      return { container: { ...base, backgroundColor: tokens.colors.primary }, pressedContainer: { ...base, backgroundColor: tokens.colors.primaryPressed }, iconColor: tokens.colors.textOnPrimary };
    case 'outline':
      return { container: { ...base, backgroundColor: 'transparent', borderWidth: tokens.layout.borderWidth, borderColor: tokens.colors.borderStrong }, pressedContainer: { ...base, backgroundColor: tokens.colors.surfaceMuted, borderWidth: tokens.layout.borderWidth, borderColor: tokens.colors.borderStrong }, iconColor: tokens.colors.textPrimary };
    case 'ghost':
    default:
      return { container: { ...base, backgroundColor: 'transparent' }, pressedContainer: { ...base, backgroundColor: tokens.colors.surfaceMuted }, iconColor: tokens.colors.textPrimary };
  }
}

```ts
import { useMemo } from 'react';
import { useAppSettings } from '../settings/AppSettingsContext';
import { getDesignTokens, type DesignTokens } from './designSystem';

export type DesignSystem = {
  tokens: DesignTokens;
  isDark: boolean;
  direction: 'rtl' | 'ltr';
  isRTL: boolean;
  textAlign: 'right' | 'left';
  rowDirection: 'row' | 'row-reverse';
  writingDirection: 'rtl' | 'ltr';
};

export function useDesignTokens(): DesignSystem {
  const { isDark, direction } = useAppSettings();

  return useMemo<DesignSystem>(() => {
    const isRTL = direction === 'rtl';

    return {
      tokens: getDesignTokens(isDark),
      isDark,
      direction,
      isRTL,
      textAlign: isRTL ? 'right' : 'left',
      rowDirection: isRTL ? 'row-reverse' : 'row',
      writingDirection: isRTL ? 'rtl' : 'ltr',
    };
  }, [isDark, direction]);
}

export function useThemedStyles<T>(factory: (tokens: DesignTokens) => T): T {
  const { tokens } = useDesignTokens();
  return useMemo(() => factory(tokens), [factory, tokens]);
}
```

## Analysis: active Expo Router entry point

From the provided files, the active router root is **`mobile/src/app`**, not `mobile/app`:

- `mobile/package.json` uses `"main": "expo-router/entry"`.
- `mobile/app.json` enables the `expo-router` plugin and does not override the router root.
- Expo Router resolves `src/app` before `app` when both exist. Therefore:
  - **Active layout:** `mobile/src/app/_layout.tsx`
  - **Active home screen:** `mobile/src/app/index.tsx`
  - `mobile/app/_layout.tsx` and `mobile/app/index.tsx` are inactive legacy files. I left them untouched.

The active app already has a working settings/theme layer in `mobile/src/core/settings/AppSettingsContext.tsx` (`language`, `theme`, `direction`, `isDark`, `t`). I will build the design system on top of that without changing its public API, so Persian RTL, Kurdish localization, English LTR, and existing settings remain intact.

## What I’m adding

I’m adding a new, additive design-system layer:

1. **`mobile/src/core/theme/designSystem.ts`**
   - Brand, surface, border, text, and semantic colors for light/dark.
   - Typography scale, spacing, radii, icon sizes, layout constants, shadows, opacity, z-index, and motion tokens.
   - Style recipes for cards, buttons, and icon buttons.
   - No `letterSpacing` or `textTransform` in typography tokens, because those can break Persian/Kurdish cursive shaping.

2. **`mobile/src/core/theme/useDesignTokens.ts`**
   - `useDesignTokens()` derives tokens from the existing `useAppSettings()` `isDark` and `direction`.
   - Returns RTL/LTR helpers: `textAlign`, `rowDirection`, `writingDirection`.
   - `useThemedStyles()` provides memoized, direction-aware style factories.

3. **`mobile/src/core/theme/index.ts`**
   - Clean barrel export for the new design system.

No existing files are modified, deleted, or replaced. The home redesign is intentionally not implemented yet.

import type { TextStyle, ViewStyle } from 'react-native';

/**
 * GridHand design system.
 *
 * This module is additive and intentionally does not change the existing
 * AppSettingsContext API. Consumers should derive tokens through
 * `useDesignTokens()` so light/dark mode and RTL/LTR direction stay in sync
 * with the existing app settings.
 *
 * Localization note:
 * - Typography tokens intentionally avoid `letterSpacing` and `textTransform`.
 *   Both can break cursive joining in Persian and Kurdish text.
 * - Direction-aware layout values are exposed by `useDesignTokens()`.
 */

export type DesignTokens = {
  scheme: DesignColorScheme;
  colors: ThemeColors;
  typography: Record<TypographyVariant, TextStyle>;
  spacing: typeof spacing;
  radii: typeof radii;
  iconSizes: typeof iconSizes;
  layout: typeof layout;
  shadows: Record<ShadowLevel, ShadowToken>;
  opacity: typeof opacity;
  zIndex: typeof zIndex;
  motion: typeof motion;
};

export const lightTokens: DesignTokens = {
  scheme: 'light',
  colors: lightColors,
  typography,
  spacing,
  radii,
  iconSizes,
  layout,
  shadows: lightShadows,
  opacity,
  zIndex,
  motion,
};

export const darkTokens: DesignTokens = {
  scheme: 'dark',
  colors: darkColors,
  typography,
  spacing,
  radii,
  iconSizes,
  layout,
  shadows: darkShadows,
  opacity,
  zIndex,
  motion,
};

export function getDesignTokens(isDark: boolean): DesignTokens {
  return isDark ? darkTokens : lightTokens;
}

export type CardVariant = 'default' | 'elevated' | 'outlined' | 'filled' | 'accent';

export function getCardStyle(
  tokens: DesignTokens,
  variant: CardVariant = 'default'
): ViewStyle {
  const base: ViewStyle = {
    borderRadius: tokens.radii.lg,
    padding: tokens.layout.cardPadding,
  };

  switch (variant) {
    case 'elevated':
      return {
        ...base,
        backgroundColor: tokens.colors.surfaceElevated,
        ...tokens.shadows.md,
      };
    case 'outlined':
      return {
        ...base,
        backgroundColor: 'transparent',
        borderWidth: tokens.layout.borderWidth,
        borderColor: tokens.colors.borderStrong,
      };
    case 'filled':
      return {
        ...base,
        backgroundColor: tokens.colors.surfaceMuted,
      };
    case 'accent':
      return {
        ...base,
        backgroundColor: tokens.colors.accentSoft,
        borderWidth: tokens.layout.borderWidth,
        borderColor: tokens.colors.accent,
      };
    case 'default':
    default:
      return {
        ...base,
        backgroundColor: tokens.colors.surface,
        borderWidth: tokens.layout.borderWidth,
        borderColor: tokens.colors.border,
        ...tokens.shadows.sm,
      };
  }
}

export type ButtonVariant = 'primary' | 'secondary' | 'ghost' | 'danger' | 'accent';
export type ButtonSize = 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg';

export type ButtonStyleSet = {
  container: ViewStyle;
  pressedContainer: ViewStyle;
  label: TextStyle;
  pressedLabel: TextStyle;
  iconColor: string;
};

export type ButtonStyleOptions = {
  variant?: ButtonVariant;
  size?: ButtonSize;
  direction?: 'rtl' | 'ltr';
};

const buttonHeights: Record<ButtonSize, number> = {
  sm: 36,
  md: 44,
  lg: 52,
};

const buttonPadding: Record<ButtonSize, number> = {
  sm: 12,
  md: 16,
  lg: 20,
};

const buttonLabelVariant: Record<ButtonSize, TypographyVariant> = {
  sm: 'smallStrong',
  md: 'button',
  lg: 'title',
};

export function getButtonStyle(
  tokens: DesignTokens,
  options: ButtonStyleOptions = {}
): ButtonStyleSet {
  const { variant = 'primary', size = 'md', direction = 'rtl' } = options;

  const base: ViewStyle = {
    minHeight: buttonHeights[size],
    paddingHorizontal: buttonPadding[size],
    borderRadius: tokens.radii.md,
    alignItems: 'center',
    justifyContent: 'center',
    flexDirection: direction === 'rtl' ? 'row-reverse' : 'row',
    gap: tokens.spacing.sm,
  };

  const label: TextStyle = {
    ...tokens.typography[buttonLabelVariant[size]],
    textAlign: 'center',
  };

  switch (variant) {
    case 'secondary':
      return {
        container: {
          ...base,
          backgroundColor: tokens.colors.surface,
          borderWidth: tokens.layout.borderWidth,
          borderColor: tokens.colors.borderStrong,
        },
        pressedContainer: {
          ...base,
          backgroundColor: tokens.colors.surfaceMuted,
          borderWidth: tokens.layout.borderWidth,
          borderColor: tokens.colors.borderStrong,
        },
        label: { ...label, color: tokens.colors.textPrimary },
        pressedLabel: { ...label, color: tokens.colors.textPrimary },
        iconColor: tokens.colors.textPrimary,
      };
    case 'ghost':
      return {
        container: {
          ...base,
          backgroundColor: 'transparent',
        },
        pressedContainer: {
          ...base,
          backgroundColor: tokens.colors.primarySoft,
        },
        label: { ...label, color: tokens.colors.primary },
        pressedLabel: { ...label, color: tokens.colors.primaryPressed },
        iconColor: tokens.colors.primary,
      };
    case 'danger':
      return {
        container: {
          ...base,
          backgroundColor: tokens.colors.danger,
        },
        pressedContainer: {
          ...base,
          backgroundColor: tokens.colors.dangerPressed,
        },
        label: { ...label, color: tokens.colors.textInverse },
        pressedLabel: { ...label, color: tokens.colors.textInverse },
        iconColor: tokens.colors.textInverse,
      };
    case 'accent':
      return {
        container: {
          ...base,
          backgroundColor: tokens.colors.accent,
        },
        pressedContainer: {
          ...base,
          backgroundColor: tokens.colors.accentPressed,
        },
        label: { ...label, color: tokens.colors.textOnAccent },
        pressedLabel: { ...label, color: tokens.colors.textOnAccent },
        iconColor: tokens.colors.textOnAccent,
      };
    case 'primary':
    default:
      return {
        container: {
          ...base,
          backgroundColor: tokens.colors.primary,
        },
        pressedContainer: {
          ...base,
          backgroundColor: tokens.colors.primaryPressed,
        },
        label: { ...label, color: tokens.colors.textOnPrimary },
        pressedLabel: { ...label, color: tokens.colors.textOnPrimary },
        iconColor: tokens.colors.textOnPrimary,
      };
  }
}

export type IconButtonVariant = 'ghost' | 'soft' | 'solid' | 'outline';
export type IconButtonSize = 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg';

export type IconButtonStyleSet = {
  container: ViewStyle;
  pressedContainer: ViewStyle;
  iconColor: string;
};

export type IconButtonStyleOptions = {
  variant?: IconButtonVariant;
  size?: IconButtonSize;
};

const iconButtonSizes: Record<IconButtonSize, number> = {
  sm: 32,
  md: 40,
  lg: 48,
};

export function getIconButtonStyle(
  tokens: DesignTokens,
  options: IconButtonStyleOptions = {}
): IconButtonStyleSet {
  const { variant = 'ghost', size = 'md' } = options;

  const dimension = iconButtonSizes[size];

  const base: ViewStyle = {
    width: dimension,
    height: dimension,
    borderRadius: tokens.radii.md,
    alignItems: 'center',
    justifyContent: 'center',
  };

  switch (variant) {
    case 'soft':
      return {
        container: {
          ...base,
          backgroundColor: tokens.colors.primarySoft,
        },
        pressedContainer: {
          ...base,
          backgroundColor: tokens.colors.primarySoft,
          opacity: tokens.opacity.pressed,
        },
        iconColor: tokens.colors.primary,
      };
    case 'solid':
      return {
        container: {
          ...base,
          backgroundColor: tokens.colors.primary,
        },
        pressedContainer: {
          ...base,
          backgroundColor: tokens.colors.primaryPressed,
        },
        iconColor: tokens.colors.textOnPrimary,
      };
    case 'outline':
      return {
        container: {
          ...base,
          backgroundColor: 'transparent',
          borderWidth: tokens.layout.borderWidth,
          borderColor: tokens.colors.borderStrong,
        },
        pressedContainer: {
          ...base,
          backgroundColor: tokens.colors.surfaceMuted,
          borderWidth: tokens.layout.borderWidth,
          borderColor: tokens.colors.borderStrong,
        },
        iconColor: tokens.colors.textPrimary,
      };
    case 'ghost':
    default:
      return {
        container: {
          ...base,
          backgroundColor: 'transparent',
        },
        pressedContainer: {
          ...base,
          backgroundColor: tokens.colors.surfaceMuted,
        },
        iconColor: tokens.colors.textPrimary,
      };
  }
}

import { useMemo } from 'react';
import { useAppSettings } from '../settings/AppSettingsContext';
import { getDesignTokens, type DesignTokens } from './designSystem';

export type DesignSystem = {
  tokens: DesignTokens;
  isDark: boolean;
  direction: 'rtl' | 'ltr';
  isRTL: boolean;
  textAlign: 'right' | 'left';
  rowDirection: 'row' | 'row-reverse';
  writingDirection: 'rtl' | 'ltr';
};

/**
 * Derives GridHand design tokens from the existing app settings.
 *
 * This keeps the current AppSettingsContext API untouched while giving screens
 * a single, direction-aware source for colors, typography, spacing, shadows,
 * and layout values.
 */
export function useDesignTokens(): DesignSystem {
  const { isDark, direction } = useAppSettings();

  return useMemo<DesignSystem>(() => {
    const isRTL = direction === 'rtl';

    return {
      tokens: getDesignTokens(isDark),
      isDark,
      direction,
      isRTL,
      textAlign: isRTL ? 'right' : 'left',
      rowDirection: isRTL ? 'row-reverse' : 'row',
      writingDirection: isRTL ? 'rtl' : 'ltr',
    };
  }, [isDark, direction]);
}

/**
 * Memoized style factory helper.
 *
 * The factory should be defined at module scope so its identity stays stable:
 *
 * const createStyles = (system: DesignSystem) =>
 *   StyleSheet.create({ ... });
 *
 * const styles = useThemedStyles(createStyles);
 */
export function useThemedStyles<T>(factory: (system: DesignSystem) => T): T {
  const system = useDesignTokens();

  return useMemo(() => factory(system), [factory, system]);
}

export type EngineeringImageProps = {
  assetId: AssetId;
  style?: StyleProp<ViewStyle>;
  imageStyle?: StyleProp<ImageStyle>;
  borderRadius?: number;
  scrim?: 'none' | 'bottom' | 'full';
  placeholderIconSize?: number;
  children?: React.ReactNode;
};

export function EngineeringImage({
  assetId,
  style,
  imageStyle,
  borderRadius = radiusTokens.lg,
  scrim = 'none',
  placeholderIconSize = 40,
  children,
}: EngineeringImageProps) {
  const asset = getAsset(assetId);
  const [loaded, setLoaded] = useState(false);
  const opacity = useRef(new Animated.Value(0)).current;

  const handleLoad = useCallback(() => {
    setLoaded(true);
    Animated.timing(opacity, { toValue: 1, duration: 220, useNativeDriver: true }).start();
  }, [opacity]);

  const hasPhoto = asset.bundled && asset.source != null;

  return (
    <View
      style={[styles.root, { borderRadius }, style]}
      accessible
      accessibilityRole="image"
      accessibilityLabel={asset.alt}
    >
      {hasPhoto ? (
        <Animated.Image
          source={asset.source}
          resizeMode="cover"
          onLoad={handleLoad}
          style={[StyleSheet.absoluteFill, { opacity: loaded ? opacity : 0 }, imageStyle]}
          accessibilityIgnoresInvertColors
        />
      ) : (
        <Placeholder asset={asset} iconSize={placeholderIconSize} />
      )}
      ...
```

## What I'm proposing

I can't ship binary photography through a chat message, so I'm building the **system** that the imagery plugs into — plus a hard guarantee that the app looks intentional and premium *before* the photos land, and stays offline-safe and cheap on low-end Android.

**No new dependencies.** Everything uses what's already in `package.json`: `lucide-react-native` (icons), `expo-linear-gradient` (placeholder gradients), `react-native-svg` (engineering grid pattern).

### Design decisions

| Concern | Decision |
|---|---|
| **No emojis** | A single semantic icon registry (`icons.ts`) + `<Icon />` wrapper. A `node --test` guard fails CI if any emoji appears in `src/` or `app/`. |
| **Offline** | Photos are bundled via static `require()` into the APK — zero network, zero cache eviction. No remote URLs in the manifest. |
| **Low-end Android** | Bundled assets avoid runtime decode-from-network; placeholders are vector/gradient (no bitmap cost); fade-in uses `useNativeDriver`; no custom fonts. |
| **Preserve existing assets** | The manifest is purely additive. Nothing is deleted or renamed. |
| **Graceful degradation** | Every asset has a `placeholder` (gradient + icon + optional grid). Until a photo is dropped in, the UI renders a deliberate industrial placeholder — not a broken image. |

### The one manual step

Each manifest entry has `bundled: false`. When a photo is added to `mobile/assets/images/`, you flip two lines:

```ts
bundled: true,
source: require('../../../assets/images/hero-lineworker.jpg'),
```

`mobile/assets/images/README.md` documents the full shot list, dimensions, and compression budgets.

### Files

- `mobile/src/core/theme/tokens.ts` — industrial palette, spacing, radii, elevation, scrims
- `mobile/src/core/assets/icons.ts` — semantic icon registry (no emojis)
- `mobile/src/core/assets/Icon.tsx` — consistent icon renderer
- `mobile/src/core/assets/assetManifest.ts` — 18-slot engineering imagery registry
- `mobile/src/core/assets/EngineeringImage.tsx` — offline-first image with placeholder fallback
- `mobile/src/core/assets/index.ts` — barrel
- `mobile/assets/images/README.md` — art direction + drop-in procedure
- `mobile/tests/no-emoji.test.mjs` — emoji guard

`mobile/global.css`, `mobile/package.json`, and `mobile/app.json` need **no changes**.

/**
 * GridHand design tokens.
 *
 * Single source of truth for the "premium industrial" visual language:
 * graphite structure, high-voltage amber for field/safety, grid cyan for
 * data/network, conductor copper for materials.
 *
 * Deliberately dependency-free and font-free so it costs nothing on
 * low-end Android devices.
 */

export const palette = {
  // Structural neutrals (graphite / steel)
  graphite900: '#0A0F16',
  graphite800: '#111823',
  graphite700: '#1A2331',
  graphite600: '#243040',
  graphite500: '#334155',
  steel400: '#64748B',
  steel300: '#94A3B8',
  steel200: '#CBD5E1',
  steel100: '#E2E8F0',
  steel50: '#F1F5F9',
  white: '#FFFFFF',

  // High-voltage amber — field work, safety, primary action
  amber600: '#B45309',
  amber500: '#F59E0B',
  amber400: '#FBBF24',
  amber100: '#FEF3C7',

  // Grid cyan — data, network, telemetry
  cyan600: '#0E7490',
  cyan500: '#06B6D4',
  cyan400: '#22D3EE',
  cyan100: '#CFFAFE',

  // Conductor copper — materials, cables, windings
  copper600: '#9A3412',
  copper500: '#C2410C',
  copper400: '#EA580C',
  copper100: '#FFEDD5',

  // Semantic
  success500: '#16A34A',
  success100: '#DCFCE7',
  warning500: '#F59E0B',
  warning100: '#FEF3C7',
  danger500: '#DC2626',
  danger100: '#FEE2E2',
  info500: '#0284C7',
  info100: '#E0F2FE',
} as const;

export type PaletteColor = keyof typeof palette;

/** 4pt spacing scale. */
export const spacing = {
  none: 0,
  xs: 4,
  sm: 8,
  md: 12,
  lg: 16,
  xl: 20,
  '2xl': 24,
  '3xl': 32,
  '4xl': 40,
  '5xl': 48,
  '6xl': 64,
} as const;

export const radius = {
  sm: 6,
  md: 10,
  lg: 14,
  xl: 20,
  '2xl': 28,
  pill: 999,
} as const;

export const typography = {
  display: { fontSize: 30, lineHeight: 38, fontWeight: '700' },
  title: { fontSize: 22, lineHeight: 30, fontWeight: '700' },
  heading: { fontSize: 18, lineHeight: 26, fontWeight: '600' },
  body: { fontSize: 15, lineHeight: 24, fontWeight: '400' },
  label: { fontSize: 13, lineHeight: 20, fontWeight: '600' },
  caption: { fontSize: 12, lineHeight: 18, fontWeight: '400' },
  mono: { fontSize: 13, lineHeight: 20, fontWeight: '500' },
} as const;

/**
 * Elevation presets. Kept shallow on purpose — deep shadows are expensive
 * to composite on low-end GPUs.
 */
export const elevation = {
  none: {},
  sm: {
    shadowColor: palette.graphite900,
    shadowOpacity: 0.12,
    shadowRadius: 4,
    shadowOffset: { width: 0, height: 1 },
    elevation: 1,
  },
  md: {
    shadowColor: palette.graphite900,
    shadowOpacity: 0.16,
    shadowRadius: 10,
    shadowOffset: { width: 0, height: 3 },
    elevation: 3,
  },
  lg: {
    shadowColor: palette.graphite900,
    shadowOpacity: 0.22,
    shadowRadius: 18,
    shadowOffset: { width: 0, height: 6 },
    elevation: 6,
  },
} as const;

export const motion = {
  fast: 120,
  base: 200,
  slow: 320,
} as const;

/**
 * Scrims used over photography so text stays legible regardless of the
 * underlying image. Values are pre-baked rgba strings so they can be fed
 * straight into expo-linear-gradient.
 */
export const scrim = {
  bottom: ['rgba(10,15,22,0)', 'rgba(10,15,22,0.82)'] as const,
  full: [
    'rgba(10,15,22,0.65)',
    'rgba(10,15,22,0.35)',
    'rgba(10,15,22,0.85)',
  ] as const,
} as const;

export const tokens = {
  palette,
  spacing,
  radius,
  typography,
  elevation,
  motion,
  scrim,
} as const;

export type Tokens = typeof tokens;

```
/**
 * Consistent icon renderer.
 *
 * All icons share the same stroke weight and optical sizing so the UI reads
 * as one professional system rather than a grab-bag of glyphs.
 */

import React from 'react';
import { icons, type IconName } from './icons';
import { palette } from '../theme/tokens';

export type IconProps = {
  name: IconName;
  size?: number;
  color?: string;
  strokeWidth?: number;
  accessibilityLabel?: string;
};

export function Icon({
  name,
  size = 20,
  color = palette.steel300,
  strokeWidth = 1.75,
  accessibilityLabel,
}: IconProps) {
  const Glyph = icons[name];

  return (
    <Glyph
      size={size}
      color={color}
      strokeWidth={strokeWidth}
      accessibilityLabel={accessibilityLabel}
      accessibilityRole={accessibilityLabel ? 'image' : undefined}
    />
  );
}

/**
 * Engineering imagery registry.
 *
 * Every photographic asset in GridHand is declared here by semantic id. The
 * manifest is additive: adding a slot never disturbs existing assets.
 *
 * OFFLINE POLICY
 * --------------
 * Assets are bundled into the binary with a static `require()` so they are
 * available with no network and cannot be evicted from a cache. There are no
 * remote URLs in this file by design.
 *
 * DROP-IN PROCEDURE
 * -----------------
 * 1. Place the file in `mobile/assets/images/` using the `file` name below.
 * 2. Set `bundled: true`.
 * 3. Add `source: require('../../../assets/images/<file>')`.
 *
 * Until then the asset renders its `placeholder` (gradient + icon + optional
 * engineering grid), which is a deliberate design state, not a broken image.
 */

import type { IconName } from './icons';

export type AssetCategory =
  | 'lineworker'
  | 'engineer'
  | 'transformer'
  | 'substation'
  | 'network'
  | 'equipment'
  | 'safety'
  | 'abstract';

export type AssetPriority = 'critical' | 'high' | 'low';

export type AssetPattern = 'grid' | 'none';

export type AssetPlaceholder = {
  /** Two-stop gradient, fed directly to expo-linear-gradient. */
  gradient: readonly [string, string];
  icon: IconName;
  pattern: AssetPattern;
};

export type EngineeringAsset = {
  id: AssetId;
  category: AssetCategory;
  /** File name inside mobile/assets/images/. */
  file: string;
  /** True once the file exists and `source` is wired up. */
  bundled: boolean;
  /** Static require() result. Set together with `bundled: true`. */
  source?: number;
  width: number;
  height: number;
  aspectRatio: number;
  priority: AssetPriority;
  /** Always true today; kept explicit so the policy is auditable. */
  offline: boolean;
  /** Screen-reader description. */
  alt: string;
  placeholder: AssetPlaceholder;
};

export type AssetId =
  | 'hero.lineworker'
  | 'hero.substation'
  | 'lineworker.portrait'
  | 'lineworker.crew'
  | 'engineer.planning'
  | 'engineer.inspection'
  | 'transformer.distribution'

  | 'equipment.meter'

export const ASSET_IDS = Object.keys(ASSETS) as AssetId[];

export function getAsset(id: AssetId): EngineeringAsset {
  return ASSETS[id];
}

export function getAssetsByCategory(category: AssetCategory): EngineeringAsset[] {
  return ASSET_IDS.map((id) => ASSETS[id]).filter((asset) => asset.category === category);
}

/** Assets that must be bundled for the app to be usable offline. */
export function getOfflineCriticalAssets(): EngineeringAsset[] {
  return ASSET_IDS.map((id) => ASSETS[id]).filter(
    (asset) => asset.offline && asset.priority !== 'low',
  );
}

mobile/src/core/assets/EngineeringImage.tsx
```
/**
 * Offline-first engineering image.
 *
 * - Bundled photos render from the binary (no network, no cache eviction).
 * - Missing or failed photos render a deliberate industrial placeholder
 *   (gradient + engineering grid + semantic icon) instead of a broken image.
 * - Fade-in is driven on the native thread so it stays smooth on low-end
 *   Android hardware.
 */

import React, { useCallback, useRef, useState } from 'react';
import {
  Animated,
  StyleSheet,
  View,
  type ImageStyle,
  type StyleProp,
  type ViewStyle,
} from 'react-native';
import { LinearGradient } from 'expo-linear-gradient';
import Svg, { Defs, Pattern, Path, Rect } from 'react-native-svg';

import { getAsset, type AssetId, type EngineeringAsset } from './assetManifest';
import { Icon } from './Icon';
import { radius as radiusTokens, scrim as scrimTokens } from '../theme/tokens';

export type ScrimMode = 'none' | 'bottom' | 'full';

export type EngineeringImageProps = {
  assetId: AssetId;
  style?: StyleProp<ViewStyle>;
  imageStyle?: StyleProp<ImageStyle>;
  borderRadius?: number;
  /** Dark gradient overlay so overlaid text stays legible. */
  scrim?: ScrimMode;
  placeholderIconSize?: number;
  children?: React.ReactNode;
};

type LoadStatus = 'loading' | 'ready' | 'error';

export function EngineeringImage({
  assetId,
  style,
  imageStyle,
  borderRadius = radiusTokens.lg,
  scrim = 'none',
  placeholderIconSize = 40,
  children,
}: EngineeringImageProps) {
  const asset = getAsset(assetId);
  const [status, setStatus] = useState<LoadStatus>('loading');
  const opacity = useRef(new Animated.Value(0)).current;

  const handleLoad = useCallback(() => {
    setStatus('ready');
    Animated.timing(opacity, {
      toValue: 1,
      duration: 220,
      useNativeDriver: true,
    }).start();
  }, [opacity]);

  const handleError = useCallback(() => {
    setStatus('error');
  }, []);

  const hasPhoto = asset.bundled && asset.source != null;
  const showPhoto = hasPhoto && status !== 'error';

  return (
    <View
      style={[styles.root, { borderRadius }, style]}
      accessible
      accessibilityRole="image"
      accessibilityLabel={asset.alt}
    >
      {showPhoto ? (
        <Animated.Image
          source={asset.source}
          resizeMode="cover"
          onLoad={handleLoad}
          onError={handleError}
          style={[StyleSheet.absoluteFill, { opacity }, imageStyle]}
          accessibilityIgnoresInvertColors
        />
      ) : (
        <Placeholder asset={asset} iconSize={placeholderIconSize} />
      )}

      {scrim !== 'none' ? (
        <LinearGradient
          colors={scrim === 'full' ? scrimTokens.full : scrimTokens.bottom}
          locations={scrim === 'full' ? [0, 0.45, 1] : [0, 1]}
          start={{ x: 0, y: 0 }}
          end={{ x: 0, y: 1 }}
          style={StyleSheet.absoluteFill}
          pointerEvents="none"
        />
      ) : null}

      {children}
    </View>
  );
}

function Placeholder({
  asset,
  iconSize,
}: {
  asset: EngineeringAsset;
  iconSize: number;
}) {
  return (
    <View style={StyleSheet.absoluteFill}>
      <LinearGradient
        colors={asset.placeholder.gradient}
        start={{ x: 0, y: 0 }}
        end={{ x: 1, y: 1 }}
        style={StyleSheet.absoluteFill}
      />

      {asset.placeholder.pattern === 'grid' ? <GridPattern /> : null}

      <View style={styles.placeholderIcon}>
        <Icon
          name={asset.placeholder.icon}
          size={iconSize}
          color="rgba(255,255,255,0.38)"
          strokeWidth={1.5}
        />
      </View>
    </View>
  );
}

/** Faint engineering grid — vector only, negligible memory cost. */
function GridPattern() {
  return (
    <Svg style={StyleSheet.absoluteFill} width="100%" height="100%">
      <Defs>
        <Pattern id="gridhand-grid" width={24} height={24} patternUnits="userSpaceOnUse">
          <Path
            d="M 24 0 L 0 0 0 24"
            fill="none"
            stroke="rgba(255,255,255,0.10)"
            strokeWidth={1}
          />
        </Pattern>
      </Defs>
      <Rect width="100%" height="100%" fill="url(#gridhand-grid)" />
    </Svg>
  );
}

const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  root: {
    overflow: 'hidden',
    backgroundColor: '#0A0F16',
  },
  placeholderIcon: {
    ...StyleSheet.absoluteFillObject,
    alignItems: 'center',
    justifyContent: 'center',
  },
});
